instruction: I have a multi-monitor setup but I find it confusing to have different workspaces on each monitor. Can you configure the system so that workspaces are only on the primary monitor by enabling workspaces-only-on-primary?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling workspaces-only-on-primary setting in GNOME mutter to configure multi-monitor workspace behavior. When enabled (true), workspaces are only created on the primary monitor, and secondary monitors show windows from all workspaces. The setup sets workspaces-only-on-primary to false (workspaces on all monitors), and the task asks the user to enable it to true (workspaces only on primary). Evaluator verifies the setting is changed to true using exact_match metric with vm_command_line getter.
metadata.verification: Verified by checking gsettings mutter workspaces-only-on-primary - the setting is a boolean that controls multi-monitor workspace behavior. When true, workspaces are only on the primary monitor; when false, workspaces appear on all monitors. The task requires toggling from false to true.

llm_judge_reasons: Perfect semantic alignment: Instruction asks to enable 'workspaces-only-on-primary' and evaluator checks exactly that setting via 'gsettings get org.gnome.mutter workspaces-only-on-primary'.
Correct getter logic: The vm_command_line getter executes the gsettings command which directly retrieves the boolean setting value, returning 'true\n' when enabled.
Correct expected value: Expected value 'true\n' matches the exact output format of 'gsettings get' for a boolean true value.
Appropriate metric: exact_match is the correct metric for comparing a gsettings boolean output, as it requires exact string match including the newline character.
Complete coverage: The evaluator checks the only requirement in the instruction - that the workspaces-only-on-primary setting is enabled (changed from false to true).
Correct setup: The setup config correctly sets the initial state to false (workspaces on all monitors), and the task requires changing it to true (workspaces only on primary monitor).

Semantically correct setting: The workspaces-only-on-primary setting correctly controls whether workspaces appear on all monitors (false) or only the primary monitor (true), which directly addresses the user's stated problem of finding it 'confusing to have different workspaces on each monitor'.
